query:
Industry: bakery operations dashboard
Client brief: Hearth bakery operations dashboard. A shift lead needs todays bake quantities, oven status, low stock and collection orders. Dense but calm, warm paper and brick red, usable real controls. Product demo data must be labelled. No marketing hero or invented business growth claims.
Audience: bakery shift leads
Primary action: review todays bake and update production
Brand colours: #F5F3EE, #292B28, #963D28
Subject objects: bake quantities, oven status, stock, collection orders
No marketing hero.
No growth claims.

matched_industry.name: Dashboards, Analytics & Admin Software
matched_industry.layout_archetype: Collapsible Command Sidebar + KPI Strip + Filterable Data Table & Chart Canvas
matched_industry.first_viewport_priority: Actionable status summary, anomaly highlights, keyboard-navigable filter/command bar

palette.notes: Brief colours #F5F3EE, #292B28, #963D28 lead: #F5F3EE is the ground; #963D28 as accents; #292B28 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents | base High-scannability semantic tokens with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`

conversion_trust_elements: Clear empty, loading, and error states
matched_industry.motion_language: Fast 120ms state transitions, skeleton shimmer loaders, zero decorative scroll animations
anti_patterns: Oversized marketing hero inside an authenticated dashboard
Giant padding that forces horizontal scrolling

category_cliches: A row of four KPI cards over one line chart
Cream background with a terracotta accent and an italic serif
Template hero (headline left, illustration right, two buttons)
Uniform card grids with icon + heading + paragraph
Gradient blobs and glassmorphism with no brand reason
distinctiveness.instruction: Subject first: list the objects, tools and moments a visitor actually sees in this business (a bakery: loaves, the oven, flour; an optician: frames, lenses, the test chart). The first screen must show the most characteristic of them as authored art at scale, so a stranger can name the business with the text covered. Then write down 3 concrete references from the brand's own world (local architecture, craft traditions, signage, landscape, the material itself) and derive palette, pattern, and type voice from them. Materials: paper, oven — sample real colours and textures from them. The clichés below are generic *treatments* (layouts, kits, palettes), not the subject's own objects: avoid the treatments, never the subject.

brief_signals.brief_action: review todays bake and update production

matched_styles.name: Atelier Tactile Minimalism
characteristics: Warm paper and limestone neutrals (`#FAF8F5`) rather than sterile `#FFFFFF`
Unhurried vertical rhythm (`96px–140px` section spacing) and monograph captions
Zero decorative card wrappers; imagery and typography sit directly on the canvas

matched_styles.name: Crisp Product Workbench
characteristics: Interactive live product state demonstrations in the hero instead of static screenshots
Subtle surface layering (`#FCFCFA` -> `#F2F3EE`) with crisp 1px borders
Clear scannable feature proof and transparent pricing architecture

matched_styles.name: High-Density Operational Cockpit
characteristics: Compact 4px/8px/12px spacing grid maximizing above-the-fold data visibility
Right-aligned `tabular-nums` numeric columns, keyboard-first filtering, and clear status badges
Complete empty, loading, error, and overflow-resilient states

directions.title: Direction A — Dashboards, Analytics & Admin Software (Live Status Board)
directions.layout_composition: Bakery operations dashboard opens on live status: one line says whether the service is normal, then a map or list of today's numbers with current issues and planned work (units, timestamps, owners and status); the exception list and the plan table follow; 'resolve what is late or short' is a prominent report button. Structure: a live status strip and map, then planned work, then how to report. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity medium; accent on cells and rows that need action. Mobile: the status line is first; the map follows at half height
directions.visual_identity: Control room: Plus Jakarta Sans for the status line, Inter for details, JetBrains Mono for references and times; palette brand-f5f3ee-292b28-963d28-on-workbench-slate (light ground): brief colours #f5f3ee, #292b28, #963d28 lead: #f5f3ee is the ground; #963d28 as accents; #292b28 as surfaces and deep tones, never accents; status colours are the only colours; corners: 2px on controls and cards, square images (hairline-2); body 1rem (16px) minimum, labels and captions 0.75rem (12px) minimum; fallbacks Plus Jakarta Sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; Plus Jakarta Sans: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif

directions.content_treatment: Is it working, where is it not, when will it be fixed, how do I report it
directions.motion_choreography: No motion: today's numbers and every section render in their final state on load; hover and focus change colour only; nothing moves on scroll

hero_frame.build: One giant figure, date or price leads; the headline sits small beneath it, proof first.

flow.build: Numbered rows that open in place to reveal each section, like a chapter index.

section_head.build: Each head is a visitor's question in plain words; the answer starts right below.

ground.build: Soft gradients drifting between two pale tints of the palette; no hard bands.

material.build: Diagrams and technical drawings: plans, exploded views, flow lines and callouts.

labels.build: A short accent dash before each label, body face semibold, sentence case.

motion.build: Micro motion only: hover, focus and press states (150-200ms), no scroll choreography; signature: check-tick (Web Animations API). Reduced motion: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every effect is replaced by its final state; all content stays visible and readable.

motion_techniques.build: Form checks and toggles tick with a 160ms stroke draw.

motif.build: Bezel frame: media sits inside a thin, even bezel with one continuous corner radius, like the housing of today's numbers; the same radius and bezel width carry to panels and the primary button. Nothing is drawn over the media.

button.build: Primary: solid accent fill, 52px tall with 28px side padding, radius 10px (the bezel's inner radius), label at medium weight; hover deepens the fill one step (150ms), press sinks it 1px, and keyboard focus shows a 2px accent ring offset 3px. Secondary: a button of the same size with a 1px outline (translucent white on dark grounds, ink at 30% on light ones) that fills on hover.

restraint: No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings, and no tiny tracked caps anywhere.
No monospace face: figures use the body face's tabular numerals.
No index numerals (01, 02) on sections or steps; an ordered list carries order.
No gradients, glows, glass panels or blobs: flat colour chapters carry the page.
No icon cards and no row of three or more identical cards: vary size, span and media per item.
At most two typefaces; hierarchy comes from size and weight.
One h1, authored in at most two lines at every width; statements stay under about 25 words.
Sections 120-240px apart on desktop (about clamp(88px, 11vw, 168px)); never cramped bands.
Real pictures of the trade's objects wherever the brief supplies them, four or more; no stock filler or placeholder art.
One live interaction born from the product (its deciding spec made interactive) with a no-JS table of the same facts.
The footer returns the brand line large across the full width.

workflow_guidance: BRIEF COLOURS: the brief names its own colours (#F5F3EE, #292B28, #963D28). Use them as the palette in every direction (check WCAG pairs); the direction palettes below are fallbacks only.

Mode A (New Website): the user's prompt wins over everything here. The 3 directions are structural raw material (layout, content treatment, dials), not finished looks; the visual world comes from art direction.

DISTINCTIVENESS: Read `distinctiveness` first. If `match_confidence` is `none` or `weak`, the industry profile is only a fallback; build the visual world from the brief's place and material cues instead, and do not ship any listed category cliché unless the brief asks for it.

ART DIRECTION (load `skills/layoza-art-direction`): commit to ONE specific world. Derive the world from far (place, notation, print traditions), keep the subject up close (the trade's object as the signature interaction, at scale), rule out the category reflex and its obvious opposite, and put the visitor's real action in the first viewport. Let colour own whole sections. Decide motion and tools per design; nothing is mandatory.

ENGINEERING LESSONS: sticky headers need `html { scroll-padding-top: <header height + 1rem> }` (WCAG 2.4.11); web fonts need metric-adjusted fallback `@font-face` (size-adjust / ascent-override) or the font swap re-wraps headings and fails CLS; scroll reveals must end visible.

HERO: Layoza does not fix the first-screen composition; you choose it, from the subject and the brief. The directions suggest full-bleed / layered / centred (each with its reason in `rationale`), and the dealt hero mechanic is one fit for that composition, not the only one. Give the three directions three different first screens, do not default to headline-left / visual-right (a split needs a stated reason), and record `HERO:` with the reason in `.layoza/direction.md`.
TYPE & LEADING: Keep multi-line display headings at `line-height >= 1.0` so ascenders and descenders never collide.

LAYOUT SAFETY: Keep short header links/buttons on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), give side-by-side heading columns >= 16px of clear space, collapse multi-column grids before gaps exceed the viewport, and size any <canvas> from a fixed-size container with devicePixelRatio capped at 2.
Verify in a real browser with `layoza qa <file-or-url>` (1440/768/375): it measures contrast, overflow, clipping, nav, scroll reveals, and lab Core Web Vitals; fix every error.

DIRECTIONS: render three materially different compositions with identical factual content and available assets at desktop and phone sizes. Compare the actual renders for hierarchy, typography, image integration, clarity and full-page rhythm. Choose with reasons as the designer unless the user asked to choose. Persist candidates, screenshot evidence and visible tradeoffs with review_design; never invent user approval. Library deals are starting material, not mandatory shapes or a substitute for art direction.

PAGE SHAPE: each direction's `page_shape` is a set of suggestions, not orders. Decide every axis (hero frame, flow, section heads, ground, material, labels, motion level and tools) from this brief's facts; keep a suggestion only when it serves your concept, and record each decision with its reason in .layoza/direction.md. Axes in `pinned_by_prompt` follow the user's words; whatever you choose stays unique against the ledger.

FORM: for each page or section answer narrative role, viewing distance, visual temperature, content capacity and visual motif before styling it; at delivery add one line per section saying which content the form came from.

COPY: specific nouns from the brief, no startup clichés, no invented metrics, reviews or logo walls (use honest placeholders such as `[customer quote — to supply]`), and call-to-action verbs taken from what the visitor actually does.

SELF-CRITIQUE before QA: score philosophy, hierarchy, execution, specificity, restraint, variety from 1 to 5; any score below 3 means revise first. Put the stamp `/* layoza · direction: <A|B|C> · structure: <style_family> · hero: <hero id> · palette: <palette id> · type: <type id> · critique: P4 H4 E4 S4 R4 V4 */` as the first line of the main CSS (your direction, structure, hero, palette, type and scores).

concepts.composition: The bakery operations dashboard as a command-first console: one centred command bar with suggestions drawn from today's numbers and the exception list; results open as panels beneath; shortcuts are shown on every action. Structure: one command bar, suggestions, result panels, visible shortcuts. Knobs: density standard; span irregularity low; accent on the active control and its result. Mobile: the command bar docks to the bottom above the keyboard; results stack full width
concepts.why_this_subject: Command-First Console for "bakery operations dashboard" (productui surface): expert users repeat a few jobs many times a day and type faster than they click. Type Urbanist / Urbanist (low-contrast geometric) for a utility voice, tagged calm/data like the brief. Palette brand-f5f3ee-292b28-963d28-on-proofing-basket on a light ground, tagged warm-grain/calm like the brief. First screen: centred composition, hero material live-ui, look family swiss-grid, corners tool-6. Motion flavour (tier and tools follow page_shape.motion): palette open and filter transitions. Licence: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Brand first: palette built around the brief's colours (#F5F3EE, #292B28, #963D28). Other structures that fit this slot: Component Playground, Catalogue Index, Plain Index Page, Timeline Axis.

client_request: Hearth bakery operations dashboard. A shift lead needs todays bake quantities, oven status, low stock and collection orders. Dense but calm, warm paper and brick red, usable real controls. Product demo data must be labelled. No marketing hero or invented business growth claims.
craft_floor: Header: one row, 52-72px tall on desktop and 56-76px on mobile; logo 24-40px high on the left, 4-6 nav links of 15-16px at weight 500 with 24-40px between them, the primary action on the right at the header's button size. Phone or hours sit in that row or the footer; no utility bar stacked above the nav. Mark the current link with a 2px underline 6px below the text; a sticky header turns opaque after the first scroll, never taller.

Primary button: 36-52px tall, horizontal padding 20-32px (about twice the vertical), label 15-17px at weight 600 in sentence or title case with tracking 0-0.02em, at most one drawn SVG icon of 16-20px set 8px from the label. The secondary action matches its height, radius and padding as an outline (1-1.5px) or ghost; one button shape and radius on the whole page, 44px minimum hit area everywhere.

Button states, all four authored: :hover shifts the fill by 6-10% lightness or nudges the icon 2-4px; :active presses with translateY(1px) or scale(0.98) over 80-120ms; :focus-visible draws a 2px ring at 2-3px offset with at least 3:1 contrast; disabled sits at 45-55% opacity with cursor not-allowed. No state changes width, height or padding.

Type scale: at most 10 distinct font sizes each carry 2% or more of the text on a desktop render, each step at least 1.2x the one below; body 14-17px at line-height 1.5-1.65; headings at line-height 1.0-1.15. The h1 tops out at 88px on desktop (set with clamp()), and display sizes of 48px and up track -0.02 to -0.04em, never tighter than -0.05em; body text keeps tracking at 0.
Measure: prose never runs past 82 characters a line (cap paragraphs at 60-68ch with max-width); h1 lines stay under 20ch and h2 under 24ch; no centred paragraph runs past three lines.

Spacing rhythm: every gap comes from one 4/8px scale. Sections pad 80-144px top and bottom on desktop and 64-96px on mobile; a heading sits 16-24px above its text and has at least twice that space above it; content width caps at 1200-1320px with 24-40px gutters on desktop and 16-20px on mobile.

Section heads: one heading per section (one h2, or the h1 in the hero) and at most one lead paragraph of 40 words or fewer. No stacked pile of label, heading, accent-coloured second heading and paragraph; a second voice goes in the body, not the head.

Composition: no two neighbouring sections share a layout; use 4 or more layout kinds across the page (split, full-bleed media, list or table, asymmetric grid, quote, form). Card rows vary span or media; never a grid of equal cards that differ only by text.

Hero: the h1, one supporting paragraph of 30 words or fewer, at most two actions and one real picture or film; at most 16 text blocks in the first viewport. Spec tables, chip rows and stat grids go below the fold (one slim proof strip may sit on the fold line). On a 390x844 phone a real picture is in view before the first scroll.

Imagery: real photographs or renders of the trade's own objects, one aspect ratio per row (16:9, 3:2, 4:3 or 1:1) with object-fit: cover, corner radius from the button's family. Nothing decorative over a product picture: no hairlines, crosshairs, hotspot squares or graph-paper grids. Text on a photo sits on a scrim that holds 4.5:1; captions 13-14px in the muted ink.

Colour: one accent on no more than about 10% of any screen (primary action, links, one highlight); neutrals tinted toward the accent hue, never pure grey; at most two ground colours plus one accent ground across the page; body and secondary text at 4.5:1 or better, large text at 3:1.

Icons: one drawn SVG set at one stroke weight (1.5 or 2px) and one size per context (16, 20 or 24px), coloured with currentColor. Never a Unicode arrow, check mark, star or emoji standing in for an icon.

Motion: one signature moment; every other transition runs 120-250ms ease-out on transform and opacity only. Reveals travel 24px or less, start from content that is already readable, and differ by section role rather than one fade-up everywhere. No infinite loops besides hero media; prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off.

Footer: brand and one-line description, two or three link groups and the contact block, four columns at most on desktop; group titles 13-14px at weight 600 in sentence case; links 15-16px with 10-12px between rows; a bottom bar for legal and copyright at 13-14px; 64px or more of top padding.

Browser surfaces: ::selection and focus rings use the palette; link underlines sit 3-4px below the text at 1-2px thickness; tables and figures use tabular numerals; no unthemed default blue links anywhere.
Technical: figures in tabular numerals, real UI or diagrams instead of illustration, monospace only for actual code, radii 4-8px, nothing animates longer than 250ms.

Craft: warm photography of hands, materials and the place in natural light, 3 or more real pictures above the footer, no stock; type with some character in the headings and a plain body; prices and opening hours are text, not images.
